stages.choice_rule: Four single words. Exactly one completes the blank. Always include the partner homophone. Add a third form from the same set when one exists (to/too/two, there/their/they're). Last slot is a look-alike. Never a second grammatical fit. Use they're, you're, it's with apostrophes.

gold_items.stem: The kids left blank bag at school.
I blank the right way home.
<NAME> does not know blank or not we should wait.
<NAME> said blank ready to play outside.

roots: Keep four one-word choices and never reorder a fixed label set, because labels change per item.
The partner homophone must appear in every choice set.
No other choice may make a real sentence in the blank.
Tier 1 far words are short and obviously wrong (hat, ten, sit).
Tier 3 must show the full common set or close wh- look-alikes.
Do not write picture clues in the stem.
Stay in school, home, food, pets, play, family, or weather.

tier_rules.1: Stems of four to six words. Easy pairs: hear/here, see/sea, to/too/two. Far distractors plus the partner. Add a lemma picture for a concrete noun.
tier_rules.2: Stems of five to eight words. Grade 2 pairs: their/there/they're, write/right, know/no, your/you're. Partner plus one look-alike.
tier_rules.3: Stems of seven to ten words. Near misses: whether or not, they're vs their/there. Two-syllable words are fine. Only one choice can fit.

hear_here.en: Hear means to listen. Here means this place.

see_sea.en: See means to look. Sea means the ocean.

to_too_two.en: To means toward. Too means also or very. Two means the number 2.

their_there_theyre.en: Their means it belongs to them. There means a place. They're means they are.
their_there_theyre.ko: Their는 그들의 것입니다. There는 장소입니다. They're는 they are입니다.

write_right.en: Write means to make words. Right means correct or the right side.
write_right.ko: Write는 글을 쓴다는 뜻입니다. Right는 맞다 또는 오른쪽입니다.

know_no.en: Know means you have the fact. No means not yes.
know_no.ko: Know는 안다는 뜻입니다. No는 아니라는 뜻입니다.

weather_whether.en: Weather means rain or sun. Whether means if or which way.

your_youre.en: Your means it belongs to you. You're means you are.
your_youre.ko: Your는 너의 것입니다. You're는 you are입니다.

one_won.en: One means the number 1. Won means you came in first.

ate_eight.en: Ate means you finished food. Eight means the number 8.

for_four.en: For means meant for someone. Four means the number 4.

by_buy.en: By means next to or how. Buy means to get with money.
by_buy.ko: By는 옆에 또는 '~로'입니다. Buy는 산다는 뜻입니다.

hole_whole.en: Hole means an opening. Whole means all of it.

blew_blue.en: Blew means the wind moved it. Blue is a color.
blew_blue.ko: Blew는 바람이 불었다는 뜻입니다. Blue는 파란색입니다.

sun_son.en: Sun is the bright star. Son is a boy in a family.

be_bee.en: Be means to exist. A bee is a bug that buzzes.

our_hour.en: Our means it belongs to us. An hour is a time of day.
our_hour.ko: Our는 우리의 것입니다. Hour는 한 시간입니다.

new_knew.en: New means not old. Knew means you already had the fact.
new_knew.ko: New는 새것이라는 뜻입니다. Knew는 알고 있었다는 뜻입니다.

through_threw.en: Through means from one side to the other. Threw means you tossed it.
through_threw.ko: Through는 통과한다는 뜻입니다. Threw는 던졌다는 뜻입니다.

flower_flour.en: A flower grows in a garden. Flour is used to bake.

week_weak.en: A week is seven days. Weak means not strong.
week_weak.ko: Week는 일주일입니다. Weak는 힘이 없다는 뜻입니다.

meat_meet.en: Meat is food from an animal. Meet means to see someone.

wood_would.en: Wood comes from a tree. Would talks about a wish or plan.
wood_would.ko: Wood는 나무입니다. Would는 바람이나 계획에 쓰입니다.

night_knight.en: Night is the dark time. A knight is a person in armor.

red_read.en: Red is a color. Read means you looked at words.

plane_plain.en: A plane flies in the sky. Plain means simple or not fancy.

sail_sale.en: Sail means a boat moves on water. Sale means a lower price.
sail_sale.ko: Sail은 배가 가는 것입니다. Sale은 할인 판매입니다.

wear_where.en: Wear means to put on clothes. Where asks about a place.
wear_where.ko: Wear는 옷을 입는 것입니다. Where는 장소를 묻습니다.

its_contraction.en: Its means it belongs to it. It's means it is.
its_contraction.ko: Its는 그것의 것입니다. It's는 it is입니다.

mail_male.en: Mail is a letter. Male means a boy or man.

road_rode.en: A road is a street. Rode means you went on a bike or horse.
